newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Uighurs face 7-day detention in Kazakhstan -exiles.
newsitem.headline: Uighurs face 7-day detention in Kazakhstan -exiles.

text.p: More than 20 ethnic Uighurs face seven days in police custody after being detained in the Kazakh capital Almaty for protesting near the Chinese embassy, a Uighur organisation in exile said on Tuesday.

"The 24 people detained on Monday near the Chinese embassy have been given seven days detention for disturbing the peace," Yusupbek Mukhlisi, leader of the Almaty-based United Revolutionary Front of Eastern Turkestan, told Reuters.
Kazakh security officials could not immediately be reached and a duty officer at the interior ministry refused to comment.
Monday's protest was against executions of Uighur separatists in China's Xinjiang province last week.
Mukhlisi, whose son Mukhiddin is among those detained and is the separatist group's spokesman, said about 30 demonstrators had been detained but nine were released soon afterwards.
Xinjiang, a remote region of desert and mountains in northern China which is home to the Uighurs and other Turkic-speaking peoples, has a long history of ethnic friction.
A demonstration by people demanding Xinjiang's independence last February in the town of Yining, near the border with Kazakhstan, turned violent. Nine people were killed and 198 were hurt.
A Xinjiang official said on Monday Chinese paramilitary police had shot dead two people in the province last week when a mob of more than 100 tried to rescue convicted rioters from execution.
Officials in Xinjiang said three Uighurs were executed last week.
Kazakhs and Uighurs share a common religious, linguistic and cultural heritage but the former Soviet republic is under pressure from China to clamp down on the activities of Uighur exile groups.
